Empirical Research Plan: “Long-run Effects of Regulation-Induced TSPs Reductions on Adult and Elderly Mortality, 1969–1974”

-----------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-----------------------------------------------------
Preferred approach: Difference-in-Differences (DID) panel design, augmented with an instrumental-variables (IV) second stage to translate the policy-generated pollution change into a causal mortality elasticity.

Why DID?  
• The Clean Air Act created a plausibly exogenous treatment—“nonattainment” status—applied in 1972 according to a federal TSPs threshold.  
• We observe counties for multiple pre-policy years (1969–71) and multiple post-policy years (1972–74), allowing county and year fixed effects to difference out time-invariant county attributes and nationwide shocks.  
• Parallel-trend diagnostics can be run with pre-policy data.  

Why add IV?  
• Nonattainment status may affect mortality through channels other than pollution (e.g., plant closures that change income).  
• Using the interaction Nonattainment × Post as an instrument for the actual TSPs change isolates the pollution pathway, delivering a causal TSPs–mortality gradient.

-----------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-----------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable
  TREAT_ct  = 1 if county c is designated “nonattainment” for TSPs and year t ≥ 1972; 0 otherwise.

Control group
  • Counties classified “attainment” for TSPs (never subject to the stricter abatement mandate).

Treatment timing
  • Start of 1972 (EPA list published January 31, 1972).  
  • Post period = 1972–1974. Pre period = 1969–1971.

Instrument (first stage)
  Z_ct  = Nonattainment_c × Post_t

Outcome variables
  • ln(MortRate_50plus_ct): log all-cause deaths per 100,000 among age ≥50.  
  • ln(MortRate_65_84_ct): ditto for age 65–84.

Running variable & cutoff
  • Not applicable for the main DID; however, in robustness we will implement a local RDD around the 75 µg/m³ geometric-mean threshold.

-----------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-----------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends (DID): In the absence of the policy, mortality in attainment and nonattainment counties would have evolved similarly.  
Plausibility: EPA used a mechanical pollution threshold, not health or mortality data, to set status. Pre-1972 mortality trends can be tested.

A2. Exclusion (IV step): Conditional on controls and county×year fixed effects, Nonattainment × Post affects mortality only through its effect on TSPs.  
Plausibility: Biggest concern is economic shocks from regulation; we will control for county-year economic covariates and show robustness excluding highly industrial counties.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers): Pollution abatement in one county does not substantially change mortality in neighboring attainment counties (or migration is limited).  
Plausibility: TSPs are relatively localized; we will test for spillovers by adding neighbors’ treatment status as a control.

-----------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification and Remedies
-----------------------------------------------------
T1. Differential pre-trends.  
  Remedy: Event-study plot of coefficients for each pre-policy year; include county-specific linear trends as robustness.

T2. Economic shocks caused by regulation (plant closures, income loss) that independently affect mortality.  
  Remedy:  (i) Control flexibly for BEA income, earnings, transfer payments, employment composition.  
           (ii) Use IV approach so that only the within-county variation in TSPs driven by regulation identifies the health effect.

T3. Selective migration of older individuals out of dirtier (nonattainment) counties post-1972.  
  Remedy:  (i) Use mortality rates per resident population so that denominator adjusts;  
           (ii) Show that county-age population counts do not differentially trend post-policy;  
           (iii) Re-estimate with state×year fixed effects to soak up broad migration patterns.

-----------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline (executable)
-----------------------------------------------------
```r
# Load libraries
library(data.table)   # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)       # high-performance fixed-effects estimation
library(ivreg)        # 2SLS (alternative: feols with iv)
library(ggplot2)

#---------------------------
# 5.1 Data loading
#---------------------------
mort <- fread("mortality_by_county_age_race_gender.csv")   # deaths & population
poll <- fread("county_ann_tsp.csv")                       # mean TSPs, exceedances
econ <- fread("bea_county_econ.csv")                      # income, employment, etc.
status <- fread("epa_attainment_status.csv")              # attainment indicator

#---------------------------
# 5.2 Variable construction
#---------------------------
# Merge
dat <- Reduce(function(x,y) merge(x, y,
                                  by = c("county_fips","year"),
                                  all = TRUE),
              list(mort, poll, econ, status))

# Mortality rates
dat[, mort_50p := deaths_50p / pop_50p * 1e5 ]
dat[, mort_65_84 := deaths_65_84 / pop_65_84 * 1e5 ]
dat[, ln_mort_50p := log(mort_50p) ]
dat[, ln_mort_65_84 := log(mort_65_84) ]

# Treatment variables
dat[, post := as.integer(year >= 1972)]
dat[, nonattain := as.integer(status_tsp == "nonattainment")]
dat[, treat := post * nonattain]          # DID term (also the IV)

#---------------------------
# 5.3 Main DID regression
#---------------------------
did_main <- feols(ln_mort_50p ~ post + nonattain + treat |
                    county_fips + year,
                  data = dat, cluster = ~county_fips)
summary(did_main)

#---------------------------
# 5.4 IV: Effect of TSPs on mortality
# First stage
fs <- feols(TSP_mean ~ treat + post + nonattain |
              county_fips + year, data = dat,
            cluster = ~county_fips)
summary(fs)

# Second stage 2SLS
iv_main <- feols(ln_mort_50p ~ 1 | county_fips + year |
                   (TSP_mean ~ treat) ,
                 data = dat, cluster = ~county_fips)
summary(iv_main)

#---------------------------
# 5.5 Event-study (parallel trends check)
#---------------------------
dat[, rel_year := year - 1972]  # event time
event <- feols(ln_mort_50p ~ i(rel_year, nonattain, ref = -1) |
                 county_fips + year,
               data = dat[year <= 1974 & year >= 1969],
               cluster = ~county_fips)
iplot(event) + theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Pre-trend test: Adult mortality")

#---------------------------
# 5.6 Robustness: include county-specific linear trends
#---------------------------
did_trend <- feols(ln_mort_50p ~ treat + post + nonattain |
                     county_fips[year] + year,
                   data = dat, cluster = ~county_fips)
summary(did_trend)
```

-----------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-----------------------------------------------------
Direction: A decline in TSPs should reduce cardiorespiratory and all-cause mortality, so coefficients are anticipated to be negative.

Magnitude (rough prior): Historical epidemiologic elasticity suggests that a 10 µg/m³ fall in long-run TSPs might lower annual all-cause mortality for the 65–84 cohort by roughly 1–2%. With a baseline of ~2,000 deaths per 100,000 in that age range, this implies ~20–40 fewer deaths per 100,000 per 10 µg/m³ reduction.

-----------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID/IV)
(1 = clearly satisfied; 0 = questionable/absent)
-----------------------------------------------------
C1. No differential pre-trends in outcome ............. 1  
C2. Treatment exogeneity (assignment independent) ..... 0.8  
C3. No simultaneous shocks differentially correlated ... 0.7  
C4. Stable composition/no selective sorting ........... 0.7  
C5. No interference/spillovers between units .......... 0.8  

Overall, assumptions appear plausible but economic-shock and migration channels warrant careful robustness analysis.
